checks.name: The library uses only its environment-specific browser preference record
A new environment starts with no browser history or bookmarks
Actual hard limits remain history 200 and bookmarks 100
250 visits retain exactly the latest 200 unique entries
Saved history contains URL/title/time only
Revisiting moves one URL to the front and updates its title
Bookmark caller limits cannot exceed the actual 100-entry cap
Bookmark writes preserve the independent history collection
A smaller caller limit retains exactly its newest three entries
A nonpositive caller limit still yields a bounded one-row record
Missing or empty titles fall back to the URL
Invalid and credential-bearing addresses never enter persistence
Malformed preference recovers to an empty list: not-json
Malformed preference recovers to an empty list: {}
Malformed preference recovers to an empty list: null
Malformed preference recovers to an empty list: [broken
Restoration drops nonobjects, missing/unsafe URLs and duplicate entries
Read-only cleanup never rewrites old preference bytes
The next actual visit persists only repaired valid rows
Oversized restored arrays obey each collection's cap
Raw records beyond two MiB are rejected before JSON processing
A valid visit recovers from an oversized old record
Mutating a returned list cannot mutate serialized preference storage
Arbitrary website titles are bounded to 300 UTF-16 units
Truncation never cuts a surrogate pair at the boundary
A complete surrogate pair fitting exactly at the limit is preserved
Restored old long titles receive the same bounded cleanup
Bookmark membership reads actual saved records
Removing a bookmark leaves other bookmarks and history intact
Removal eliminates every restored duplicate of the selected URL
Clearing history removes only its storage key
Removing an absent URL preserves valid remaining records
Reopening the same environment recalls the serialized bookmark collection
Different supplied environment contexts cannot see each other's collections
Writing or clearing one context does not change the other environment
Unknown collection names cannot read arbitrary preference records

scope: Complete production BrowserLibrary, BrowserAddressPolicy and J. Explicit in-memory Context/SharedPreferences/Editor adapters supply separate environment stores; actual ProfileContext, Android persistence scheduling, Chromium/Gecko, page content, DNS and network are not executed. Workloads cover 250 history visits, 130 bookmarks, hard/caller caps, recency/dedup/removal, malicious or malformed old records, two-MiB input rejection, title/surrogate bounds and serialized-storage independence.
